blocks.text: Surrey Duplexes & Half-Duplexes — Frequently Asked Questions

parts.t: What is the difference between a half-duplex and a full duplex in Surrey?

A half-duplex is one individually titled strata lot (one side of a two-unit building) that can be bought, financed, and sold separately. A full duplex consists of both dwellings on a single freehold title (or both strata lots sold together), giving one buyer ownership of the entire building and land.
Do half-duplexes in Surrey pay monthly strata fees?

Most Surrey half-duplexes operate as two-unit "non-collecting" strata corporations with no formal monthly strata fee; instead, the two owners split shared building insurance, roof upkeep, and shared-driveway maintenance (commonly 50/50 by unit entitlement). Always verify building insurance and any written agreements before removing conditions.

Can a half-duplex in Surrey have a legal basement suite?

Yes, where City of Surrey zoning and building-code fire/sound separation requirements are met. Many newer three-level half-duplexes in Grandview Heights, Pacific Douglas, and Cloverdale include a registered 1- or 2-bedroom basement suite. See
How does BC Bill 44 (SSMUH) affect duplex zoning in Surrey?

Provincial Small-Scale Multi-Unit Housing legislation requires municipalities to permit 3 to 6 units on qualifying single-family and duplex lots inside the Urban Containment Boundary, expanding infill duplex, triplex, and fourplex options across Surrey.
How is insurance handled on a two-unit strata half-duplex?

Under the BC Strata Property Act, the strata corporation (the two duplex owners together) must maintain full-replacement property insurance on the entire structure and common property, while each owner carries a separate strata-homeowner policy covering interior improvements, personal contents, and deductible assessments.
